rows.author: D029
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INTERCONNECT THROUGH THE INTERNET ALL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES, PROVINCES, CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes the interconnection through the internet of all government agencies, provinces, cities and municipalities all over the country to solve this perennial problem of lack of communication facility.  A faster and efficient dissemination of information and participation in the discussion of important issues affecting not only the country but also in their locality would then ensue.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-09-27

rows.author: D029
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FREE MEDICINE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR THE POOR AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Free Medicine Assistance Act of 2001". There is hereby established a Free Medicine Assistance Program, hereinafter referred to as the "Program," to be administered by the Department of Health through its authorized government hospital in each particular congressional district, to be known as the health district, in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development. >The Program shall be limited to eligible beneficiaries to be identified by the Department of Health through thegovernment hospital in the health district in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development. The implementing rules and regulations shall see to it that the intended beneficiaries come from the ranks of the poorest of the poor, tthe Program being strictly a poverty alleviation measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-09-27

rows.author: D029
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE PARALLEL TRANSLATION IN THE FILIPINO LANGUAGE OF THE LABELS, INSTRUCTIONS AND LITERATURES OF DRUGS AND MEDICINES MANUFACTURED, DISTRIBUTED OR SOLD IN THE PHILIPPINES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: This Act shall cover all the drugs and medicines that are manufactured, distributed or sold within the territory of the Republic of the Philippines. >It shall be mandatory for all manufacturers and distributors in the Philippines to provide a parallel translation in the Filipino language of all the labels, instructions and literatures in the bottle, box or pack of drugs and medicines before sale to the public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-09-27

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING CIVIL SERVICE ELIGIBILITY TO CONTRACTUAL OR CO-TERMINUOUS GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE RENDERED A TOTAL OF FIVE(5) YEARS OF EFFICIENT SERVICE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: In 1990, Republic Act No. 6850 was passed granting civil service eligibility to govenrment employees appointed under provisional or temporary status who have rendered a total of seven (7) years. The law left out contractual and co-terminous government employees from the opportunity to acquire a permanent status, Likewise in 1995 barangay health workers who have rendered five years of continuous service was granted civil service eligibility through Republic Act No. 7883.> If these group of government employees were given such privilege, the same may also be extended to other groups of similar status in accordance with the equal protection clause as guaranteed by the Constitution.

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 13, 40, 48, 52, 54 AND 99 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to RECOGNIZE the Canon Laws of the Roman Catholic Church, as well as the laws of other Christian religious organizations or denominations, pertaining to the marriage performed and celebrated according to the rites of the Church and the dissolution of the same. A marriage that has been declared to be null and void by the Roman Catholic Church through the marriage tribunal is not recognized as controlling or decisive under our civil law. The spouses whose marriage has been declared null and void by the said tribunal are therefore not free to remarry under our civil law.> The amendments to the Family Code as proposed in this bill, therefore, seeks to recognize the CHURCH's DECLARATION OF NULLITY in deciding cases pertaining too marriage and the annulment of the same, as well as in determining the legitimacy of children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-09-27

rows.author: D032
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED EIGHTEEN HUNDRED AND SIXTY-NINE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS PAGCOR CHARTER ENTITLED "CONSOLIDATING AND AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED 1067-A, 1067-B, 1067-C, 1399 AND 1632, RELATIVE TOTHE FRANCHISE AND POWERS OF THE PHILIPPINE AMUSEMENT AND GAMING CORPORATION (PAGCOR) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES"
rows.abstract: This bill, seeks, among other things to: (1) Allow PAGCOR to operate in ECONOMIC ZONE established by law; (2) Fund LIVELIHOOD PROGRAMS; (3) Create INTEGRATED recreation and sports DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS. > This bill likewise proposes amendments related to (1) Program's CORPORATE POWERS; (2) powers and functions of the Board of Directors; (3) Scope of franchise; and (4) tax incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2001-09-27

rows.author: C012
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, ENTITLED `AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE AND ESTABLISHING THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY OFFICE, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend the Intellectual Property Code through the integration of comprehensive, swift, efficient and adequate strategies designed to respond to the criminal onslaught of Internet piracy. At the same time, it seeks to give as much concern to the rights of performers, phonogram producers and broadcasters in the same breath as those accorded authors of artistic and literally works, by acknowledging the right of such phonogram producers, performers or broadcasters to control or becompensated for the various ways in which their works are used or enjoyed by others. This measure also seeks to recognize rights to distribution and rental, and rights to receive payments for certain forms of broadcasting or communication to the pubblic.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-09-27

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR AN INTEGRATED MAGNA CARTA OF TEACHERS AND NONTEACHING PERSONNEL
rows.abstract: This piece of legislation seeks to respect and fulfill the rights of teachers and non-teaching personnel in all schools in the Philippines. More particularly, it guarantees their rights to self-organizati on and to collective bargaining in accordance with ILO Conventions numbered 87 and 98. It also grants teachers' and employees' organizations whether independent or federated, the right to negotiate directly with school owner's organizations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-09-27

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROHIBIT AND PENALIZE THE USE OF CERTAIN PORTABLE ELECTRONIC DEVICES ON BOARD PHILIPPINE AIR CARRIERS WHETHER COMMERCIALLY OR PRIVATELY-OWNED AND/OR-OPERATE D FLYING OVER PHILIPPINE AIRSPACE
rows.abstract: It shall be unlawful for any person to operate at all times any portable electronic devices which transmit radio signals while in the aircraft. These include, but are not limited to amateur radio transceivers, citizens band radios, pagers, cellularphones, text messaging devices, remote control devices, other electronic devices and all other types of portable radio transceivers, whose operation in flight the carrier or commercial operator hereafter determined may likewise endanger the safety offlight. An aircraft is in flight from the moment all its external doors are closed following embarkation until any of such doors are opened for disembarkation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-09-27

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROHIBIT THE USE OF OWWA EMERGENCY REPATRIATION FUND FOR THE REPATRIATION OF UNREGISTERED AND ILLEGAL OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS (OFWs), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 15 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), in coordination with appropriate international agencies, shall undertake repatriation of REGISTERED AND LEGAL workers in cases of war, epidemic, disasters of calamities, natural or man-made, and other similar events without prejudice to reimbursement by the responsible principal or agency. However, in cases where the principal or recruitment agency cannot be identified, all costs attendant to repatriation shall be borned by the OWWA.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-09-27

rows.author: C020
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-04-23, transmitted to on 2002-04-29 and received by the Senate on 2002-04-30
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE REGULATORY FUNCTIONS OF THE PHILIPPINE OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT AGENCY (POEA) IN REGARD TO FILIPINO OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE THE DEREGULATION AND PHASE-OUT PROVISIONS OF SECTIONS 29 AND 30 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8042, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MIGRANT WORKERS AND FILIPINO OVERSEAS ACT OF 1995, AND FOR OTHER PUR POSES
rows.abstract: The entire deregulation and phase-out provisions of Sections 29 and 30 of Republic Act No. 8042 is hereby repealed.> Deregulation will reduce government's responsibility to that of a provider of information regarding the situation of the receiving country where an OFW intends to work, and in case the OFW still decides to work overseas, the responsibility to protect his or her rights is left in the hands of the OFW himself or herself.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04279

rows.author: C065
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-11-19, transmitted to on 2003-11-20 and received by the Senate on 2003-12-01
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CERTAIN TOURISM-ORIENTE D BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS TO SECURE ACCREDITATION FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM AS A PREREQUISITE TO THE ISSUANCE OF LICENSE OR PERMIT TO OPERATE BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to make accreditation by the Department of Tourism mandatory for certain major tourism-oriente d establishments, specifically hotels, resorts, tourist inns, motels, apartels, tour guiding agencies, tour transport operators, travel agencies, tour operators and professional congress organizers, prior to the issuance of permit or license to operate by the respective LGUs. It aims to strengthen the coordination between the Department of Tourism and the local government units with the end in view of making tourism establishments in the country meet world class standards.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06082

rows.author: D031
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING ADVERTISEMENTS OF LIQUOR AND ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES, CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS IN PRINT, ELECTRONIC AND BROADCAST MEDIA, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All advertisements of liquor and alcoholic beverages shall contain the advise: "GOVERNMENT WARNING" EXCESSIVE ALCHOL INTAKE MAY RESULT IN LIVER DISEASE AND DEATH." or its translation in Filipino or other dialects, such advise occupying not less thanten percent (10%) of the total area of the advertisement for print and outdoor advertising.> All advertisements of cagarettes and tobacco products shall contain a warning statement not less than ten percent (10%) of the total area of the advertisement for print and outdoor advertising stating: "GOVERNMENT WARNING: CIGARETTE SMOKING IS DANGEROUS TO YOUR HEALTH" or its translation in Filipino and other dialects.> This bill, likewise, states the PROHIBITIONS related to said advertisements.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950
